subject: Pilot runway: add days vs credit buckets for Blue Harbor POC
messages:
From: Simon Park <simon.park@blueharbor.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: Blue Harbor Analytics Procurement <procurement@blueharbor.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — pilot runway extension or credits?

Alex — thanks again for the demo last week. We’ve been ramping the POC over the last 10 days and have pushed more ingestion than expected. Attached is a short usage report so you can see where we spiked (BH-POC-usage-report.csv).

Two quick asks:
- Can we extend the 30-day pilot by +14 calendar days? Our internal stakeholders want a little more time to validate edge cases.
- Alternatively, do you offer a small top-up credits package we can buy to cover the extra token usage without moving the end date?

If you can outline pricing and any legal/admin steps, that would be great — we’re hoping to stay in the current evaluation bracket and avoid committing to annual terms yet.

Thanks,
Simon Park
Director, Data Platforms
Blue Harbor Analytics
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Park <simon.park@blueharbor.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pilot runway extension or credits?

Hi Simon — really glad the POC is getting traction and thanks for the usage file, that helps. I ran this by our commercial motion and have three clean options you can pick from quickly: (numbers are list-price estimates before any discretionary adjustment)

1) 14-day timebox extension (no change to SKU): $4,200 flat for the full 14 days — preserves the current baseline model & routing, no change in billing cadence.
2) Credit top-up: buy a 50K-token credit pack for $2,800 that we apply to the existing pilot usage; useful if you only need to cover burst traffic. Unused credits expire at pilot end.
3) Short-term committed runway: convert to a 3-month pilot with small commit (equivalent to ~$6,000/mo) — lower unit token pricing and extended support SLAs; requires a quick SOW.

I attached a SOW draft that reflects option 1 and 3 (BlueHarbor_POC_SOW_draft.pdf). If you want option 1 we can do a lightweight amendment and DocuSign it; option 2 can be fulfilled by invoice and one-line acceptance.

If you’re ok, I’ll loop in our Sales Manager for final approval on a small concession — we can likely offer a 10–15% one-time concession on the flat extension if you sign within 72 hours.

Suggested next steps:
- Reply with preferred option.
- If option 1: I’ll send the amendment + DocuSign link.
- If option 2: I’ll raise an invoice and provision the credits immediately.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick ask — pilot runway extension or credits?  (internal)

Alex — quick internal note on commercial flex for Blue Harbor (deal BH-2026-0421):
- We can approve a one-time discretionary concession up to 15% off the flat 14-day extension fee provided there are no additional compute commitments and the customer signs the amendment and confirms no change to the data residency controls.
- If they want the 3-month committed runway, escalate to me and I’ll set a formal discount band; that requires legal review and a brief security attestation addendum.

For the timebox extension, include a DocuSign link and mark the amendment as “pilot extension — no model commit”. I’ll authorize the billing team to prioritize the invoice if Alex requests the credit top-up route instead.

Laura Bennett
Sales Manager, SMB Accounts
Redwood Inference

If you prefer the credit top-up instead, the 50K-token pack is $2,800 and I can issue that immediately instead of sending the amendment — you’ll just need to confirm.

For convenience: DocuSign link — https://www.docusign.com/exec/redwood/BH-2026-0421 (live for 7 days)
HubSpot deal (internal reference) — https://hubspot.redwood.example/deal/BH-2026-0421

Please reply with a quick confirm and I’ll send the doc or invoice. Appreciate the close collaboration — excited to see the remaining edge-case validation results.
